correctness.rationale: For a size-r down-spin set, cut=3r−2e(S), M=18−2r and H/J=27−2 cut−(h/J)M. Independently reproduced the complete cut-size by magnetization histograms by traversing all 262144 spin assignments per graph in Gray order, updating the cut from the three neighbors of each flipped vertex. The resulting minima and multiplicities match all 20 displayed entries; checking every rational line intersection and every intervening interval (including the unbounded tail) gives exposed (M, intercept) pairs (2,−21),(18,27) and (0,−19),(4,−15),(18,27). The only positive changes are h/J=3 and h/J=1,3 respectively. At zero the first has one state at each of M=−2 and 2, and the second four at M=0. At 1 the second has counts 4,42,36 at M=0,2,4. At 3 the histograms give every listed sector and totals 2495 and 2473. Cubicity also gives H/J=−27+4e(S) at h/J=3 for every spin assignment, so these are precisely the independent-set totals. Graph identities independently checked via edge-preserving relabelings to the 2004 primary facial walks and agreement of automorphism group orders 8 and 4 with Sage's documented convention. Sage's first is the genus-two graph called the 'Blanuša double' by Orbanić et al.; Sage's second is their genus-one 'Blanuša snark'. This naming distinction does not change the frozen result, which specifies Sage order and exact edges.
residual_risks: Exact finite, labeled, classical zero-temperature configurations for the two specified graphs; no thermodynamic-limit or nonzero-temperature implication.

value.rationale: The original 18-vertex cubic snark pair is a canonical same-order comparison with common degree, girth and edge-coloring obstruction. Their qualitatively different zero-field magnetization and finite-field onset give a specific separation on frustrated finite graphs, and the full magnetization-resolved degeneracy census is an exact benchmark beyond just identifying the last critical field. This value is graph-specific, not a claim to have invented the method or found a thermodynamic phase transition.
residual_risks: Finite pair result, not a general characterization of snarks.
